D'Angelo Russell was born on February 23, 1996.
D'Angelo Russell is nicknamed "DLo".
D'Angelo Russell is an American professional basketball player.
D'Angelo Russell plays for the Los Angeles Lakers of the National Basketball Association (NBA).
D'Angelo Russell was selected as a McDonald's All-American in 2014.
D'Angelo Russell played college basketball for the Ohio State Buckeyes.
D'Angelo Russell was selected second overall in the 2015 NBA draft by the Lakers.
D'Angelo Russell plays point guard.
D'Angelo Russell was named to the NBA All-Rookie Second Team with the Lakers in 2016.
D'Angelo Russell was traded to the Brooklyn Nets in 2017.
D'Angelo Russell received his first All-Star selection in 2019.
D'Angelo Russell joined the Golden State Warriors via a sign-and-trade deal in the 2019 off-season.
D'Angelo Russell was then traded to the Minnesota Timberwolves at the 2020 trade deadline.
D'Angelo Russell was traded back to the Lakers at the 2023 trade deadline.
D'Angelo Russell attended Central High School in Louisville, Kentucky as a freshman from 2010-2011.
D'Angelo Russell transferred to Montverde Academy in Montverde, Florida for his sophomore season.
D'Angelo Russell helped Montverde win back-to-back High School National Tournament championships playing alongside Ben Simmons in 2014.
D'Angelo Russell played in the McDonald's All-American Game and Jordan Brand Classic.
D'Angelo Russell committed to Ohio State on June 7, 2013.
D'Angelo Russell chose Ohio State over Louisville, Michigan State, and North Carolina.
D'Angelo Russell was rated by Rivals.com as a five-star recruit.
D'Angelo Russell played one season of college basketball for the Ohio State Buckeyes.
On January 9, 2015, D'Angelo Russell recorded a career-high 14 rebounds in a win over Maryland.
On January 21, 2015, D'Angelo Russell scored a career-high 33 points in a win over Northwestern.
On February 8, 2015, D'Angelo Russell recorded a triple-double with 23 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists against Rutgers.
During the NCAA Tournament, D'Angelo Russell scored 28 points in an overtime win over VCU.
D'Angelo Russell earned the Jerry West Award during his college career.
D'Angelo Russell was named a consensus first-team All-American.
D'Angelo Russell was named first-team All-Big Ten.
D'Angelo Russell was named Big Ten Freshman of the Year.
In 35 games for Ohio State in 2014-15, D'Angelo Russell averaged 19.3 points, 5.7 rebounds, 5.0 assists and 1.6 steals per game.
On April 22, 2015, D'Angelo Russell declared for the NBA draft, forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.
On June 25, 2015, D'Angelo Russell was selected by the Los Angeles Lakers with the second overall pick in the 2015 NBA draft.
In his debut for the Lakers on October 28, 2015, D'Angelo Russell recorded four points, three rebounds and two assists in just under 26 minutes in a loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves.
On December 4, 2015, D'Angelo Russell recorded his first career double-double with 16 points and 10 rebounds in a loss to the Atlanta Hawks.
On January 7, 2016, D'Angelo Russell scored 11 of his 27 points in the fourth quarter against the Sacramento Kings.
D'Angelo Russell participated in the 2016 Rising Stars Challenge.
In the Lakers' season opener on October 26, 2016, D'Angelo Russell scored 20 points in a win over the Houston Rockets.
On November 15, 2016, D'Angelo Russell scored a then season-high 32 points in a win over the Nets.
D'Angelo Russell missed time between November and January with knee and calf injuries.
On January 31, 2017, D'Angelo Russell recorded his second career double-double with 22 points, a career-high 10 assists and seven rebounds against the Denver Nuggets.
On February 2, 2017, D'Angelo Russell set a new career high for assists with 11 against the Washington Wizards.
On March 19, 2017, D'Angelo Russell scored a career-high 40 points in a loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers.
On June 22, 2017, D'Angelo Russell was traded, along with Timofey Mozgov, to the Brooklyn Nets in exchange for Brook Lopez and the rights to Kyle Kuzma, the 27th pick in the 2017 NBA draft.
In a 2019 interview on ESPN's First Take, Magic Johnson admitted that D'Angelo Russell's Snapchat incident with Nick Young played a role in his decision to trade Russell.
On October 18, 2017, D'Angelo Russell had 30 points and five assists in a loss to the Indiana Pacers.
On October 31, 2017, D'Angelo Russell scored a season-high 33 points in a loss to the Phoenix Suns.
On November 17, 2017, D'Angelo Russell underwent arthroscopic surgery on his left knee and was ruled out indefinitely.
On January 19, 2018, D'Angelo Russell returned to action against the Miami Heat after missing 32 games.
On January 19, 2018, D'Angelo Russell played 14 minutes in a win over the Miami Heat and went 0-for-5 from the field.
On January 31, 2018, D'Angelo Russell scored 22 points in a win over the Philadelphia 76ers.
On February 14, 2018, D'Angelo Russell recorded 18 points and nine assists off the bench against the Indiana Pacers.
On February 22, 2018, D'Angelo Russell started for the first time since November 11 and scored 19 points on 7-of-16 shooting in a loss to the Charlotte Hornets.
On February 27, 2018, D'Angelo Russell had a 25-point effort against the Cleveland Cavaliers.
On March 13, 2018, D'Angelo Russell scored 24 of his 32 points in the first quarter against the Toronto Raptors.
D'Angelo Russell's 24 points in the first quarter were the most by a Net in the opening period since Vince Carter's 24 on April 4, 2005, against Boston.
On March 23, 2018, D'Angelo Russell recorded his first career triple-double with 18 points, 13 assists and 11 rebounds against the Toronto Raptors.
D'Angelo Russell's triple-double was the first for the Nets since Terrence Williams had one against Chicago on April 9, 2010.
On November 12, 2018, D'Angelo Russell made a career-high nine 3-pointers and scored 31 points in a loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves.
On November 25, 2018, D'Angelo Russell had his highest scoring total with the Nets, recording 38 points, eight assists and eight rebounds in a loss to the 76ers.
On December 18, 2018, D'Angelo Russell had 22 points and a career-high-tying 13 assists against his former team the Los Angeles Lakers.
On January 2, 2019, D'Angelo Russell scored 22 points and 13 assists in a win over the New Orleans Pelicans.
On January 14, 2019, D'Angelo Russell scored 18 of his 34 points in the third quarter against the Boston Celtics.
On January 18, 2019, D'Angelo Russell matched his career high with 40 points in a win over the Orlando Magic.
D'Angelo Russell was subsequently named Eastern Conference Player of the Week for games played from Monday, January 14, through Sunday, January 20.
On February 1, 2019, D'Angelo Russell received his first All-Star selection as a replacement for the injured All-Star Victor Oladipo in the 2019 game.
On February 11, 2019, D'Angelo Russell recorded 28 points and a career-high 14 assists against the Toronto Raptors.
On February 13, 2019, D'Angelo Russell scored 14 of his 36 points in the third overtime against the Cleveland Cavaliers.
On February 23, 2019, D'Angelo Russell tied a career high with 40 points in a win over the Hornets.
On March 19, 2019, D'Angelo Russell scored 27 of his career-high 44 points in the fourth quarter against the Sacramento Kings.
D'Angelo Russell also had four 3-pointers in the fourth quarter, breaking Allen Crabbe's single-season franchise record of 201 3-pointers.
On March 25, 2019, D'Angelo Russell had 39 points, nine rebounds and eight assists against the Portland Trail Blazers.
The Nets finished the regular season as the sixth seed in the Eastern Conference with a 42-40 record.
In Game 1 of the Nets' first-round playoff series against the Philadelphia 76ers, D'Angelo Russell scored 26 points to lead Brooklyn to a win.
On June 28, 2019, the Nets extended a qualifying offer to D'Angelo Russell in order to make him a restricted free agent.
On July 7, 2019, D'Angelo Russell, Shabazz Napier, and Treveon Graham were traded to the Golden State Warriors as part of a sign-and-trade package for Kevin Durant.
On November 8, 2019, D'Angelo Russell scored a career-high 52 points on 37 shots in a loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves.
During his lone season with the Golden State Warriors, D'Angelo Russell averaged a career-high 23.6 points per game.

On February 6, 2020, D'Angelo Russell was traded to the Minnesota Timberwolves along with Jacob Evans and Omari Spellman for Andrew Wiggins, a 2021 protected future first-round draft pick (Jonathan Kuminga), and a future second round draft pick.
D'Angelo Russell is close friends with Karl-Anthony Towns.
On February 6, 2020, D'Angelo Russell debuted for the Minnesota Timberwolves against the Toronto Raptors.
On February 23, 2020, D'Angelo Russell sat out a game to rest his sore knee due to it being nationally televised on NBA TV.
On February 24, 2022, D'Angelo Russell led the Timberwolves to a win over the Memphis Grizzlies by scoring a season-high 37 points and nine assists.

In the Play-In game on April 12, 2022, D'Angelo Russell scored 29 points to lead the Timberwolves to victory against the Los Angeles Clippers after Karl-Anthony Towns fouled out with seven minutes left.
On November 13, 2022, D'Angelo Russell scored a season-high 30 points and delivered 12 assists in a win over the Cleveland Cavaliers.
On February 9, 2023, D'Angelo Russell was traded back to the Los Angeles Lakers as part of a three-team trade involving the Utah Jazz.
On February 11, 2023, D'Angelo Russell made his return to the Lakers in a win over the Golden State Warriors and scored 15 points, five rebounds, and six assists.
On April 28, 2023, D'Angelo Russell recorded a career playoff high 31 points in a win against the Memphis Grizzlies in the Western Conference First Round of the 2023 NBA Playoffs.
On November 29, 2023, D'Angelo Russell scored 35 points and nine assists in a win over the Detroit Pistons.
On December 9, 2023, D'Angelo Russell and the Lakers won the inaugural season of the NBA In-Season Tournament.
On January 13, 2024, D'Angelo Russell scored a then season-high 39 points and delivered eight assists in a loss to the Utah Jazz.
On January 29, 2024, D'Angelo Russell was fined $15,000 for kicking the game ball into the spectator stands after a win over the Golden State Warriors.
On March 8, 2024, D'Angelo Russell scored a season-high 44 points and delivered nine assists in a win against the Milwaukee Bucks.
On March 22, 2024, D'Angelo Russell broke Nick Van Exel's record for most three-pointers made in a single season by a player in Lakers franchise history with 184.
